- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.6) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce overshoot by 10–15% to avoid overreacting to short-term momentum.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤-0.4) and forecast is falling, avoid excessive downward bias — adjust downward only if recent price action confirms trend, otherwise revert to mean.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if the last 3–5 days show strong mean reversion (price moving back toward 60–65 range), model should not overcorrect beyond 1–2% from recent low.  
- When sentiment swings sharply (e.g., from +0.8 to -0.6), model should lag 1–2 days in adjusting forecast to avoid “sentiment lag” error.  
- If forecast peaks after a spike and sentiment remains neutral or slightly positive, reduce peak height by 5–10% to account for volatility decay.  
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, if sentiment is consistently positive over 5+ days, model should not assume sustained breakout — add a 1–2% downward buffer to avoid overconfidence.
